:::{#cor-chain-qf}

#### Vector chain rule for quadratic forms

If $\vec\eps = \vec\eps\sparen{\vb}$ is an $n \times 1$ vector-valued function
of the $p \times 1$ vector $\vb$,
with continuous partial derivatives, then

$$
\underbrace{\deriv{\vb}{\paren{\vec\eps\sparen{\vb}\cdot \vec\eps\sparen{\vb}}}}_{p \times 1}
= \underbrace{\paren{\deriv{\vb}\vec{\eps}\sparen{\vb}}}_{p \times n}
\underbrace{\paren{2 \vec\eps\sparen{\vb}}}_{n \times 1}
$$

:::

::: proof
Apply @thm-chain-vec with $\vx = \vb$, $\vy = \vec\eps$, $q = n$,
and $z = f(\vec\eps) = \vec\eps \cdot \vec\eps = \tp{\vec\eps}\vec\eps$:

$$
\ba
\deriv{\vb}\paren{\vec\eps \cdot \vec\eps}
&= \paren{\deriv{\vb}\vec\eps} \deriv{\vec\eps}\paren{\tp{\vec\eps}\vec\eps}
&& \text{(vector chain rule)}
\\
&= \paren{\deriv{\vb}\vec\eps} \paren{2\vec\eps}
&& \text{(derivative of a simple quadratic form, in } \vec\eps \text{)}
\ea
$$

The second step is @cor-deriv-normsq,
applied to the $n \times 1$ vector $\vec\eps$ in place of $\vb$.
:::

{{< slidebreak >}}

:::{#exm-chain-qf-residuals}
#### Derivative of the residual sum of squares

Let $\vy$ ($n \times 1$) and $\mX$ ($n \times p$) be constant with respect to $\vb$,
and let $\vec\eps(\vb) = \vy - \mX\vb$ be the residual vector (@def-residual).
By @thm-deriv-linear-map, $\deriv{\vb}(\mX\vb) = \tp{\mX}$,
and $\deriv{\vb}\vy = \matr{0}_{p \times n}$ because $\vy$ is constant,
so $\deriv{\vb}\vec\eps = -\tp{\mX}$ ($p \times n$).
By @cor-chain-qf:

$$
\ba
\deriv{\vb}\paren{\vec\eps \cdot \vec\eps}
&= \paren{-\tp{\mX}} \paren{2\vec\eps}
&& \text{(vector chain rule for quadratic forms)}
\\
&= -2\,\tp{\mX}\paren{\vy - \mX\vb}
&& \text{(substitute } \vec\eps = \vy - \mX\vb \text{)}
\ea
$$

Setting this $p \times 1$ vector to $\vzero$ gives the normal equations
$\tp{\mX}\mX\vb = \tp{\mX}\vy$ of least squares.

:::
